arxiv-2204-12619.title: Decoding noisy messages: a method that just shouldn’t work
arxiv-2204-12619.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . This paper is about receiving text messages through a noisy and costly line. Because the line is noisy we need redundancy, but because it is costly we can afford very little of it. I start by using well-known machinery for decoding noisy messages (compressed sensing), then I attempt to reduce the redundancy (using random projections), until I get to a point where I use more orthogonal vectors than the space dimension allows.

arxiv-2209-05452.title: Large-scale Evaluation of Transformer-based Article Encoders on the Task of Citation Recommendation
arxiv-2209-05452.creator: Zoran Medić, Jan Šnajder
arxiv-2209-05452.description: Abstract Recently introduced transformer-based article encoders (TAEs) designed to produce similar vector representations for mutually related scientific articles have demonstrated strong performance on benchmark datasets for scientific article recommendation. However, the existing benchmark datasets are predominantly focused on single domains and, in some cases, contain easy negatives in small candidate pools.

arxiv-2211-11348.title: Enhancing Mobile Robot Navigation Safety and Efficiency through NMPC with Relaxed CBF in Dynamic Environments
arxiv-2211-11348.creator: Nhat Nguyen Minh, Stephen McIlvanna, Yuzhu Sun, Yan Jin, Mien Van
arxiv-2211-11348.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nhat Nguyen Minh, Stephen McIlvanna, Yuzhu Sun, Yan Jin, Mien Van. In this paper, a safety-critical control strategy for a nonholonomic robot is developed to generate control signals that result in optimal, obstacle-free paths through dynamic environments. We formulate the control synthesis problem as an Optimal Control Problem (OCP) that enforces Control Lyapunov Function (CLF) constraints for system stability as well as safety-critical constraints using Control Barrier Function (CBF) with a relaxing decay rate of the barrier function.

arxiv-2404-13629.title: The Lockman–SpReSO project
arxiv-2404-13629.creator: Mauro González-Otero, Jordi Cepa, Carmen P. Padilla-Torres, Maritza A. Lara-López, J. Jesús González, Ángel Bongiovanni, Bernabé Cedrés, Miguel Cerviño, Irene Cruz-González, Mauricio Elías-Chávez, Martín Herrera-Endoqui, Héctor J. Ibarra-Medel, Yair Krongold, Jakub Nadolny, C. Alenka Negrete, Ana Ma
arxiv-2404-13629.description: Abstract Aims. In this article we perform a comprehensive study using galaxy data from the Lockman–SpReSO project, a far-infrared (FIR) selected sample of galaxies observed using optical spectroscopy. We analysed a sub-sample of star-forming galaxies (SFGs) with secure spectroscopic redshifts, mostly in the luminous infrared galaxies domain.

arxiv-2504-21759.title: Smart Environmental Monitoring of Marine Pollution using Edge AI Thanks: The authors thank the funding support of the Carl Zeiss Stiftung under the Sustainable Embedded AI project (P2021-02-009).
arxiv-2504-21759.creator: Mohamed Moursi, Norbert Wehn, Bilal Hammoud
arxiv-2504-21759.description: Abstract Oil spill incidents pose severe threats to marine ecosystems and coastal environments, necessitating rapid detection and monitoring capabilities to mitigate environmental damage. In this paper, we demonstrate how artificial intelligence, despite the inherent high computational and memory requirements, can be efficiently integrated into marine pollution monitoring systems.

arxiv-2509-05859.title: Dissociative recombination of NeH + with low-energy electrons: Multichannel quantum defect theory including non-adiabatic couplings
arxiv-2509-05859.creator: Riyad Hassaine 1 , János Zsolt Mezei 2 , Dahbia Talbi 3 , Jonathan Tennyson 4,1 , and Ioan F. Schneider 1
arxiv-2509-05859.description: Abstract A theoretical investigation of the dissociative recombination (DR) of NeH + with low-energy electrons in the regime where the process occurs without direct potential energy curve crossings is presented. The calculations are performed using multichannel quantum defect theory, incorporating non-adiabatic couplings between electronic states.

arxiv-2511-19686.title: CountXplain: Interpretable Cell Counting with Prototype-Based Density Map Estimation
arxiv-2511-19686.creator: Abdurahman Ali Mohammed 1, Wallapak Tavanapong 1, Catherine Fonder 2,3,5, Donald S. Sakaguchi 2,3,4,5
arxiv-2511-19686.description: Abstract Cell counting in biomedical imaging is pivotal for various clinical applications, yet the interpretability of deep learning models in this domain remains a significant challenge. We propose a novel prototype-based method for interpretable cell counting via density map estimation.

arxiv-2512-18138.title: The Madelung Problem of Finite Crystals
arxiv-2512-18138.creator: Yihao Zhao, Yang He, Zhonghan Hu
arxiv-2512-18138.description: Abstract The Coulomb potential at an interior ion in a finite crystal of size p p is given by a linear superposition of contributions from displacement vectors 𝐫 = ( x , y , z ) {\mathbf{r}}=(x,y,z) to its neighbors.

arxiv-2601-16759.title: Curated endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography images dataset These authors contributed equally. These authors jointly supervised this work.
arxiv-2601-16759.creator: Alda João Andrade, Mónica Martins, André Ferreira, Tarcísio Araújo, Luís Lopes, Victor Alves
arxiv-2601-16759.description: Abstract Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a key procedure in the diagnosis and treatment of biliary and pancreatic diseases. Artificial intelligence has been pointed as one solution to automatize diagnosis. However, public ERCP datasets are scarce, which limits the use of such approach. Therefore, this study aims to help fill this gap by providing a large and curated dataset.

pmc-10645286.title: Functional traits and drought strategy predict leaf thermal tolerance
pmc-10645286.creator: Justin M Valliere, Kekoa C Nelson, Marco Castañeda Martinez, Sean Tomlinson
pmc-10645286.description: Rising temperatures pose a major threat to native plant species, particularly in urban areas. We evaluated how native plants in a restored urban nature preserve responded to experimental heat stress. We found that species differed in levels of heat tolerance and that these differences can be explained by leaf traits.

pmc-11600561.title: Associations between serum levels of liver function biomarkers and all-cause and cause-specific mortality: a prospective cohort study
pmc-11600561.creator: Shunhu Ling, Haiping Diao, Guangbing Lu, Luhua Shi
pmc-11600561.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe liver plays critical roles in human health. Circulating level of liver function biomarkers may associate with the long-term and short-term mortality in general population.MethodsWe used data from US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1988–94 and 1999–2014. People aged ≥ 20 years with measured serum levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), total bilirubin (TB), and albumin (ALB) at baseline were included.

pmc-11603133.title: FMR1 genetically interacts with DISC1 to regulate glutamatergic synaptogenesis
pmc-11603133.creator: Takato Honda, Kazuki Kurita, Yuko Arai, Himani Pandey, Akira Sawa, Katsuo Furukubo-Tokunaga
pmc-11603133.description: Synaptic development and functions have been hypothesized as crucial mechanisms of diverse neuropsychiatric disorders. Studies in past years suggest that mutations in the fragile X mental retardation 1 (FMR1) are associated with diverse mental disorders including intellectual disability, autistic spectrum disorder, and schizophrenia.

pmc-12475403.title: A synthesized dataset of Pacific Arctic marine mammal occurrences (1860-2024)
pmc-12475403.creator: Sydney Waloven, Natalia Portales, Kelly Kapsar, Jianguo Liu
pmc-12475403.description: Data on marine mammals in the Pacific Arctic region are limited, variably collected over time and by multiple sources. Therefore, collation and synthesis of previously collected data, such as the dataset presented here, make these data more useful to researchers, managers, policy makers, and residents.

pmc-12549533.title: Rational emotive behavior therapy for preventing smoking initiation among school children: Addressing peer influence and social susceptibility
pmc-12549533.creator: Sari Wardani Simarmata, Azizah Batubara, Dony Darma Sagita, Erwita Ika Violina, Akhmad Syaikhu, Juliana Simangunsong

pmc-13165149.title: Suture Versus Non-Suture Closure of the Cystic Duct Orifice During Fenestrating Laparoscopic Subtotal Cholecystectomy: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
pmc-13165149.creator: Hiroto Sakurai, Kei Nakagawa, Shingo Tsujinaka, Kenichiro Yambe, Kazuhiro Takami, Noriko Kondo, Kuniharu Yamamoto, Chikashi Shibata, Yu Katayose
pmc-13165149.description: Background/Objectives: Laparoscopic subtotal cholecystectomy (LSC) can be performed using either the fenestrating or reconstituting method. In the fenestrating method, some surgeons additionally perform suture closure of the cystic duct orifice, whereas others do not. However, evidence regarding the clinical significance of suture closure remains limited. Methods: Between April 2018 and December 2023, 934 patients underwent cholecystectomy at our institution.

pmc-13355254.creator: Anton Kravchuk, Matthias May, Martin Burchardt, Ingmar Wolff

pmc-13361482.title: Occupational Moral Injury and Professional Quality of Life Among a Group of Greek Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13361482.creator: Evangelos C. Fradelos, Anna Patsopoulou, Maria Robie, Eirini Stylianou, Aikaterini Toska, Pavlos Sarafis, Ioanna V. Papathanasiou, Anna Mauroforou, Maria Saridi
pmc-13361482.description: Background: Occupational moral injury is associated with nurses’ psychological well-being, yet evidence linking it to professional quality of life remains limited, and no validated Greek version of the Occupational Moral Injury Scale (OMIS) has been available. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 301 nurses from two public hospitals in Greece.

pmc-13371542.title: Association between pre-pregnancy body mass index and neonatal outcomes in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology: a retrospective study
pmc-13371542.creator: Huili Qian, Yunyun Wang, Caiying Bai, Lina Gao, Xiaoling Liu, Jinrui Cui, Xiaohui Liu, Xiaohua Ding
pmc-13371542.description: ObjectiveART and pre-pregnancy BMI are strongly associated with neonatal outcomes, but there are fewer relevant studies. Our objective was to analyze the association between pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) and neonatal outcomes in women planning assisted reproductive technology (ART).MethodsThis was a retrospective study that included 994 ART singleton mothers who delivered in hospitals from July 2020 to June 2024.

pmc-13556378.title: 658. Smoking is associated with eating habits during development
pmc-13556378.creator: Y Yamaguchi, S Kasai, J Hasegawa, K Ikeda
pmc-13556378.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThere are individual differences in susceptibility to smoking, and multiple factors including genetic and lifestyle factors would be involved in the susceptibility. The genetic contribution of smoking is estimated from twin studies to be around 0.5. Many genetic factors, including single nucleotide variations, have been reported to be involved in smoking, but most have low effect sizes and have not been reproducible in subsequent studies.

pmc-13593009.title: Association between medial posterior tibial slope and medial proximal tibial angle with medial meniscus posterior root tears
pmc-13593009.creator: Tao Huang, Changling Du, Tao Meng, Heng Cao, Shoutao Zhang
pmc-13593009.description: Although tibial plateau morphology is recognized as a critical determinant of meniscal pathology, the specific associations of the medial posterior tibial slope (MPTS) and medial proximal tibial angle (MPTA) with medial meniscus posterior root tears (MMRTs) remain underexplored in contemporary literature. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of MPTS and MPTA on MMRTs.
